newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut Stock Exchange trade, brokerage details.
newsitem.headline: Beirut Stock Exchange trade, brokerage details.

text.p: The Beirut Stock Exchange traded just over two million shares in its first year of operations since reopening in January 1996 after a 13-year closure, a stock exchange official said.

Most of the trading occurred after September 30 when Solidere, Lebanon's biggest company, transferred its shares from a private market to the official exchange, adding life to the hitherto dull bourse.
A stock exchange document obtained by Reuters showed traded value by the 12 authorised brokerage houses totalled $131,744,588 between September 30 and December 31, 1996.
Banque Mediterranee, Lebanon's biggest bank, accounted for the biggest chunk of the value with $42,153,667, followed by Fidus SAL, a private finance house with $38,877,851.

However, Fidus topped market share rankings -- based on commissions earned -- with a 31.47 percent share. Its commissions outstripped Mediterranee's because the bank did many large trades for Solidere which carried commissions on a reducing scale.
